title: Order Completion Rate by Slice
prompt:
Implement `completion_rate(orders, city, order_type)`. Each row is a mapping with string keys `city`, `order_type`, and `status`. Filter by exact, case-sensitive equality of city and order_type. Return completed rows divided by all rows in that slice, or 0.0 when the slice is empty. A row is completed only if status equals "completed". Pending, cancelled, and unknown statuses all remain in the denominator. Count duplicate rows separately. Accept any iterable of rows, including a one-pass generator, without mutating rows. Use O(N) time and O(1) extra space.

Reconstruction assumption: each row is one observed order; the source did not specify deduplication or terminal-only eligibility. This exercise fixes an all-observed-orders denominator. Explain how pending orders and observation-window maturity affect interpretation, then outline slices and evidence you would inspect before attributing a low rate to dispatch, ETA, supply, fraud rules, or operations.

example.reasoning: The pending order contributes to the denominator but not the numerator.
